title: Traveling by car with Celestin and by bus with Armstrong
summary: Moore compares Celestin's cars, a lost drum case, to the Armstrong bus where uniforms were changed on the move; Armstrong called work his hustle.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: While we're talking about this traveling around the country, your traveling with Louie and so forth, the bands that you performed with before that, always traveled on buses or sometimes was there a caravan of automobiles, or did it depend on what they could afford?
Yes. For instance, with 'Papa' Celestin's band we traveled by cars and most of the

cars were not running too good. One day we were going from Opelika to Mobile and we tied the drums onto the car and we didn't tie them right. We have gone probably 10 miles when we found out that we had no drums on top of the car. So we had to go back and found the drums laying aside of the road in a gully.
Were they destroyed or were they in cases?

No, they were all right. just bumped. So that's one of the experiences I had with how we traveled with the different bands, you know, but most of the time that -- when I joined Louie, we went by the big bus with the uniforms hung in the back and whenever we came to a town, why we'd change uniforms -- I mean we changed our street clothes into uniforms right on the bus. We got to a point where we could stand on one foot and change uniforms.
Right on the bus while the bus was moving along.

Yeah, we'd hang up the uniforms if they looked halfway decent. Then at different points we'd meet with another uniform change that they sent from Glaser, the New York tailor shop and put these in the tailor shop to be cleaned. We existed on the road.

It was beautiful. It was hard work but happy days for me because I always wondered how long it would be before I'd be listening to that music behind Louie. Louie -- you don't fool that man. He knows when you're enjoying your work and he knows that I enjoyed my work and it was nice.

Did Louie ever get tired of, you know, the trips and the traveling and say that he wish he could be in a place for longer periods of time? How did you also feel about the traveling around? Not just with Louie but even with some of the other bands that you were with before him?

Well, Louie is one of the greats and when he plays an engagement he always calls it, 'that's my hustle' and when we're on the road, 'we're going to hustle tonight.' He doesn't begrudge going to work, he likes his work and he likes people, he likes to play to the people and we know when he's feeling good, he blows like that, too, and even when he doesn't feel good and he's tired and he blows, he's still great to hear.
